verses.1:1: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, according to the promise of life that is in Christ Jesus,
verses.1:2: to Timothy, dearest son: grace, mercy, peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
verses.1:3: I give thanks to God, whom I serve from my ancestors with a pure conscience, that without interruption I keep remembrance of you in my prayers, night and day,
verses.1:4: longing to see you, mindful of your tears, so that I may be filled with joy,
verses.1:5: receiving a reminder of that faith which is in you without pretense, which also dwelt first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I am certain that it is in you as well.
verses.1:6: For this reason I remind you to revive the grace of God that is in you through the laying on of my hands.
verses.1:7: For God did not give us a spirit of fear, but of power, of love, and of sober-mindedness.
verses.1:8: Therefore do not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me, His prisoner, but labor together for the gospel according to the power of God,
verses.1:9: who delivered us and called us with His holy calling, not according to our works, but according to His own purpose and the grace that was given to us in Christ Jesus before the times of the ages.
verses.1:10: Now, however, it has been manifested through the illumination of our Savior Jesus Christ, who indeed destroyed death and illuminated life and incorruption through the gospel,
verses.1:11: in which I was appointed a preacher, an apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles.
verses.1:12: For this reason I also suffer these things, yet I am not put to shame. For I know whom I have trusted, and I am certain that He is able to preserve my deposit until that day.
verses.1:13: Keep the pattern of sound words that you heard from me, in faith and in love in Christ Jesus.
verses.1:14: Guard the good deposit through the Holy Spirit, who dwells in us.
verses.1:15: You know this, that all who are in Asia have turned away from me, among whom are Phygelus and Hermogenes.
verses.1:16: May the Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, because he often refreshed me and was not ashamed of my chain;
verses.1:17: but when he had come to Rome, he diligently searched for me and found me.
verses.1:18: May the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord on that day. And how much he served me in Ephesus, you yourself know better.
verses.2:1: You therefore, my son, be strengthened in the grace that is in Christ Jesus,
verses.2:2: and the things that you heard from me through many witnesses, entrust these to faithful men who were qualified to teach others as well.
verses.2:3: Labor like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
verses.2:4: No one serving as a soldier for God entangles himself in worldly affairs, so that he may please Him to whom he has proved himself.
verses.2:5: For indeed, anyone who competes in a contest is not crowned unless he has competed lawfully.
verses.2:6: The laboring farmer ought first to partake of the fruits.
verses.2:7: Understand the things I am saying, for the Lord will give you understanding in all things.
verses.2:8: Be mindful that the Lord Jesus Christ has risen from the dead, from the seed of David, according to my gospel,
verses.2:9: in which I labor even to bonds, like one doing evil; yet the word of God is not bound.
verses.2:10: For this reason I endure all things on account of the elect, so that they too may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, with heavenly glory.
verses.2:11: A faithful saying: for if we have died with Him, we will also live with Him;
verses.2:12: if we endure, we will also reign with Him; if we deny Him, He also will deny us;
verses.2:13: if we do not believe, He remains faithful; He cannot deny Himself.
verses.2:14: Remind them of these things, solemnly testifying before the Lord. Do not quarrel over words, for it is useful for nothing except the subversion of those who hear.
verses.2:15: Take diligent care to present yourself approved to God, a worker not to be put to shame, handling the word of truth rightly.
verses.2:16: But avoid profane and empty talk, for they advance greatly toward ungodliness,
verses.2:17: and their speech creeps like cancer; among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus,
verses.2:18: who have fallen away from the truth, saying that the resurrection has already taken place, and have subverted the faith of some.
verses.2:19: Yet the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal: "The Lord knows who are His," and, "Everyone who names the name of the Lord must depart from iniquity."
verses.2:20: Now in a great house there are not only golden and silver vessels, but also wooden and earthen ones, and some indeed for honor, yet some for dishonor.
verses.2:21: If anyone therefore purifies himself from these things, he will be a vessel for honor, sanctified, and useful to the Lord, ready for every good work.
verses.2:22: Now flee from youthful desires, and pursue righteousness, faith, hope, love, and peace with those who call upon the Lord from a pure heart.
verses.2:23: But avoid foolish and undisciplined questions, knowing that they produce quarrels.
verses.2:24: And a servant of the Lord ought not to quarrel, but to be gentle toward all, ready to teach, patient,
verses.2:25: correcting with restraint those who resist the truth, if perhaps at some time God may grant them repentance to come to know the truth,
verses.2:26: and they may come to their senses from the snares of the devil, by whom they are held captive at his will.
verses.3:1: Now know this, that in the last days perilous times will be at hand:
verses.3:2: people will be lovers of themselves, greedy, haughty, arrogant, blasphemous, not obedient to parents, unthankful, wicked,
verses.3:3: without affection, without peace, accusers, unrestrained, fierce, without kindness,
verses.3:4: betrayers, reckless, swollen with pride, and lovers of pleasures more than of God,
verses.3:5: having indeed an appearance of godliness, yet denying its power. And avoid these people:
verses.3:6: for among them are those who make their way into houses and lead captive weak women burdened with sins, who are led along by various desires,
verses.3:7: always learning and never arriving at the knowledge of the truth.
verses.3:8: Now just as Jannes and Mambres resisted Moses, so these also resist the truth, men corrupted in mind, disqualified regarding the faith;
verses.3:9: yet they will advance no further, for their foolishness will be manifest to all, just as theirs also was.
verses.3:10: You, however, have closely followed my teaching, way of life, purpose, faith, forbearance, love, patience,
verses.3:11: persecutions, sufferings, the sorts of things that befell me in Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra: what persecutions I endured, and the Lord rescued me from all of them.
verses.3:12: And all who wish to live in a godly manner in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution.
verses.3:13: But evil men and deceivers will advance to what is worse, erring and leading into error.
verses.3:14: You, however, remain in the things that you have learned and that have been entrusted to you, knowing from whom you learned them,
verses.3:15: and that from infancy you have known the sacred writings, which are able to instruct you for salvation through the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
verses.3:16: All Scripture, divinely inspired, is useful for teaching, for reproving, for correcting, and for training in righteousness,
verses.3:17: so that the man of God may be perfect, equipped for every good work.
verses.4:1: I solemnly testify before God and Jesus Christ, who is going to judge the living and the dead, by His coming and His kingdom:
verses.4:2: preach the word, be persistent whether opportune or inopportune; reprove, implore, rebuke in all patience and teaching.
verses.4:3: For there will be a time when they will not tolerate sound teaching, but according to their own desires they will heap up teachers for themselves, itching in their ears,
verses.4:4: and they will indeed turn their hearing away from the truth, but will be turned to fables.
verses.4:5: As for you, keep watch, toil in all things, do the work of an evangelist, complete your ministry. Be sober.
verses.4:6: For I am already being poured out as a libation, and the time of my departure is imminent.
verses.4:7: I have contended in the good contest, I have completed the course, I have guarded the faith.
verses.4:8: For what remains, the crown of righteousness is stored up for me, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will render to me on that day, and not only to me, but also to those who love His coming. Hurry to come to me soon.
verses.4:9: For Demas left me, loving this age, and went away to Thessalonica;
verses.4:10: Crescens to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia.
verses.4:11: Luke alone is with me. Take Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for ministry.
verses.4:12: But I sent Tychicus to Ephesus.
verses.4:13: When you come, bring with you the cloak that I left at Troas with Carpus, and the books, but especially the parchments.
verses.4:14: Alexander the coppersmith did many evil things to me; the Lord will render to him according to his works.
verses.4:15: Avoid him yourself as well, for he strongly resisted our words.
verses.4:16: In my first defense no one stood with me, but all deserted me; may it not be charged to them.
verses.4:17: But the Lord stood beside me and strengthened me, so that through me the preaching might be completed and all the nations might hear; and I was rescued from the mouth of the lion.
verses.4:18: The Lord has rescued me from every evil work and will save me into His heavenly kingdom, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
verses.4:19: Greet Prisca and Aquila, and the house of Onesiphorus.
verses.4:20: Erastus remained in Corinth. But I left Trophimus ill at Miletus.
verses.4:21: Hurry to come before winter. Eubulus, Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brothers greet you.
verses.4:22: The Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Grace be with you. Amen.

notes.1:6: Vulgate reads "revive the grace" (resuscites gratiam) rather than the Greek "rekindle the gift."
notes.1:8: Vulgate renders Greek "share in suffering" as "labor together" (collabora), part of a consistent Vulgate motif of "labor" here and in 2:3 and 2:9.
notes.1:10: Vulgate renders Greek "appearing" as "illumination" (illuminationem), creating a direct lexical link with "illuminated" (illuminavit) later in the verse.
notes.1:12: Literally "my deposit" (depositum meum), which may refer either to what Paul has entrusted to God for safekeeping or to the gospel charge God has entrusted to Paul (cf. 1:14).
notes.1:18: Vulgate explicitly includes "to me" (mihi), absent from most critical Greek manuscripts.
notes.2:2: The Clementine Vulgate reads the imperfect "were" (erant), whereas Greek manuscripts and some Vulgate editions read the future "will be" (erunt).
notes.2:4: Vulgate adds "for God" (Deo), absent from the Greek, and renders Greek "the one who enlisted him" as "Him to whom he has proved himself" (cui se probavit).
notes.2:10: Vulgate reads "heavenly glory" (gloria cælesti) where the Greek text has "eternal glory."
notes.2:14: Vulgate turns the Greek indirect command ("not to quarrel") into a direct second-person imperative addressed to Timothy ("Do not quarrel," Noli contendere).
notes.2:22: Vulgate includes "hope" (spem) in the list of virtues, absent from the Greek text.
notes.3:7: Vulgate reads simply "never arriving," omitting "able" found in the Greek text.
notes.3:8: Vulgate preserves the name "Mambres" (also attested in Western witnesses), whereas most Greek manuscripts read "Jambres."
notes.3:13: Vulgate renders Greek "deceiving and being deceived" with the wordplay "erring and leading into error" (errantes, et in errorem mittentes).
notes.3:14: Vulgate reads "have been entrusted to you" (credita sunt tibi) rather than the Greek "have become convinced of."
notes.3:16: Unlike the Greek (which includes "and" between the two adjectives), the Vulgate omits "and," making "divinely inspired" (divinitus inspirata) modify "Scripture" directly.
notes.4:2: The Vulgate orders the three imperatives argue, obsecra, increpa ("reprove, implore, rebuke"), placing "implore" before "rebuke," whereas standard Greek editions order them "reprove, rebuke, exhort."
notes.4:5: The Clementine Vulgate adds the closing imperative Sobrius esto ("Be sober."), a Vulgate-distinct doublet reflecting the Greek verb already rendered by vigila ("keep watch") at the beginning of the verse.
notes.4:8: Vulgate diligunt is present tense ("who love") rather than the Greek perfect ("who have loved"). Native Clementine Vulgate 4:8 includes "Hurry to come to me soon" (Saints.Bible 4:9), while native 4:9 ("For Demas left me...") and 4:10 ("Crescens to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia.") map to Saints.Bible 4:10.
notes.4:18: The Vulgate reads the perfect tense Liberavit ("has rescued") rather than the Greek future ("will rescue"), pairing the Lord's past rescue with His future saving into His heavenly kingdom (salvum faciet).
notes.4:22: The Vulgate preserves the fuller title Dominus Jesus Christus ("The Lord Jesus Christ") and the closing Amen, whereas critical Greek texts read simply "The Lord" and omit "Amen."
